summary: - _e) Direct the Respondent to reimburse the legal and administrative costs incurred by the Petitioner in pursuing the instant Petition; and_ Meanwhile, the Commission directed the parties to file their advance written submissions and to continue the interim direction until the next date of hearing. During the hearing held on 19.08.2025, the parties made detailed submissions and concluded their respective arguments. The Commission permitted both sides to file their respective written submissions, if any, within two weeks, with copies to the other side, and reserved the matter for orders. - e) The Petitioner kept SECI informed of the aforesaid circumstances throughout. The Respondent has acknowledged the problems faced by the Petitioner and has made efforts to assist the Petitioner in securing the said land-related approvals for the Project. - a) The Petitioner is raising the issues of Force Majeure as a cover-up to wriggle out of the committed agreement resulting from the selection of and issue of the Letter of Award to the Petitioner for establishing the 200 MW Wind Power Project for the generation and supply of electricity to enable SECI to resell the same to UPPCL under the PSA. The signing of the PPA post-issuance of the Letter of Award was the sole responsibility of the Petitioner (Clause 3.32 of the RfS). - a) The Petitioner’s contention is that, as the PPA was not executed by the Petitioner as per the draft, forming part of the bid documents, there is no existing, concluded or binding - b) On the basis of the above development, a binding and enforceable agreement came into existence as per the draft terms and conditions of the PPA circulated in the bidding process, and the Petitioner, having accepted the terms and conditions while submitting its bid, notwithstanding the refusal of the Petitioner to sign the PPA. In the facts and circumstances of the present case, the signing of the PPA is a ministerial act and not a condition precedent to the effectiveness of the agreement which has resulted from the bidding process. - f) The Petitioner cannot claim the alleged force majeure affecting the implementation of the project as a ground for not signing the PPA. In terms of the RfS and the LoA, the PPA was required within three months (90 days) from the LoA. There was no force majeure event that impacted the signing of the PPA. The issue of an alleged force majeure event affecting the implementation of the PPA, even if, for the sake of argument, it were accepted, could have been raised only after the signing of the PPA. 13. From the submissions of the contracting parties, the following issues emerge for adjudication before the Commission: _implementation of the Project; delay in tariff adoption and approval of Power Sale Agreement by the Regulatory Commissions._ The Petitioner is accordingly seeking discharge from the obligations/liabilities, including the execution of the PPA and establishment of the project, towards the Respondents. _Per Contra,_ Respondents SECI and UPPCL submitted that the responsibility for the selection, identification, procurement, or leasing of land, and for obtaining clear possession of 100% of the land, falls within the scope of responsibility of the Petitioner and is to be exclusively undertaken by the Petitioner at its own cost and risk. Hence, the arrangement of land for setting up the project cannot be claimed as a ground for delay in signing the PPA. The inability of the contractors hired by the Petitioner is a matter exclusively between the Petitioner and its contractors and cannot be pleaded as a ground for failing to execute the PPA. Further, SECI has submitted that since the Petitioner has refused to sign the PPA with SECI within the stipulated time period, i.e. by 23.11.2021 (final time granted by SECI for signing of PPA), SECI is entitled to encash the Bank Guarantee equivalent to the amount of Earnest Money Deposit, i.e. 12,00,00,000 and the project of the Petitioner stands cancelled. UPPCL has submitted that on account of non-signing of the PPA by the Petitioner, even after being issued the LoA and after identification of such power for resale to UPPCL, constitutes a breach on the part of the Petitioner, and as such, UPPCL has suffered a legal injury on account of the refusal of the Petitioner to sign the PPA. 23. We note that as per the provisions of the RfS dated 22.02.2019, MoP guidelines dated 08.12.2017 and the Standard PPA, it was the duty of the Petitioner for selection/identification/procurement of land, getting clear possession of 100% of the land, etc. Moreover, the Petitioner was free to choose any land for implementing the project. There was no compulsion to construct the project only on the revenue land, and the Petitioner could have explored other opportunities. We also note that the financial inability of the Petitioner’s contractors cannot be the ground for non-commissioning of the project, as the inability of the contractors/agents appointed by the Petitioner to undertake the tasks is a matter entirely _13. The Commission vide letter dated 14-08-2020 asked the petitioner to submit the following document for beginning the proceedings in the matter:_ _14. In compliance of Commission's letter dated 14.08.2020, the Petitioner submitted the following documents on dated 12-11-2020:-_ 49. In view of the above discussions, we hold that no relief accrues in favour of the Petitioner on account of alleged Force Majeure events, and that the Petitioner cannot be discharged from its obligations under the RfS and LoA towards execution of the PPA. _“48. The fourth issue is regarding claim of LD without establishing the actual loss or injury caused to them._ _55. The findings of the Tribunal in Appeal No. 62 of 2013 and 47 of 2013 will apply in the present case.”_
title: Petition under Section 79(1)(f) read with section 79 (1)(a) and (b) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with the Guidelines for Tariff Based Competitive Bidding Process for Procurement of Power from Grid Connected Wind Power Projects, 2017 as amended from time to time seeking declaration of discharge from any obligation and liability to the Respondent under the Request for Selection No. SECI/C&P/WPD/1200MW/T7/RfS/022019 dated 22.02.2019, Letter of Award dated 19.06.2019 or otherwise.
